quests.sentenceWithBlank: The client postponed the launch ____ the marketing materials weren't ready in time.
quests.completedSentence: The client postponed the launch because the marketing materials weren't ready in time.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Because' gives the direct reason behind the postponement. 'So' would incorrectly reverse the logic, making the postponement the cause of the materials not being ready.
quests.nativeTip: This explains the actual reason for postponing - not an outcome, contrast, or added fact.
quests.example: The client postponed the launch because the marketing materials weren't ready in time.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: The marketing materials weren't ready in time, ____ the client postponed the launch.
quests.completedSentence: The marketing materials weren't ready in time, so the client postponed the launch.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'So' shows that the unfinished materials led to the postponement. 'Because' would only fit if the reason came after the outcome, which isn't the order here.
quests.nativeTip: This time the cause comes first, and the outcome follows - which connector introduces a result?
quests.example: The marketing materials weren't ready in time, so the client postponed the launch.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: ____ enrollment numbers had dropped for three straight years, the school board approved consolidating two campuses.
quests.completedSentence: since enrollment numbers had dropped for three straight years, the school board approved consolidating two campuses.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Since' introduces this established reason behind the consolidation decision. 'So' would reverse the logic, making the consolidation the cause of the enrollment drop.
quests.nativeTip: This clause states an already-established fact used as the basis for the board's decision - a common way this connector opens a sentence.
quests.example: since enrollment numbers had dropped for three straight years, the school board approved consolidating two campuses.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: Maria scheduled her appointment for early morning ____ she didn't want to miss any work later in the day.
quests.completedSentence: Maria scheduled her appointment for early morning because she didn't want to miss any work later in the day.
quests.grammarRule: Reason vs Purpose - because, not so that
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Because' explains her reason - not wanting to miss work. 'So that' would need a forward-looking modal verb like 'wouldn't' to properly express a purpose, which isn't how this is phrased.
quests.nativeTip: This explains her existing motivation for the choice, not a future goal she's trying to enable.
quests.example: Maria scheduled her appointment for early morning because she didn't want to miss any work later in the day.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: The developers added a dark mode option ____ users could reduce eye strain at night.
quests.completedSentence: The developers added a dark mode option so that users could reduce eye strain at night.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'So that' shows the developers' intentional goal, with 'could' expressing the enabled benefit. 'Because' would incorrectly frame this as an explanation rather than a forward-looking purpose.
quests.nativeTip: This was a deliberate design choice aimed at a specific future benefit, not an explanation of something that already happened.
quests.visualAnchor: 🌉 Clause A ──[ so that ]── Clause B
quests.example: The developers added a dark mode option so that users could reduce eye strain at night.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: The company switched to biodegradable packaging ____ reducing its environmental footprint had become a top priority for leadership.
quests.completedSentence: The company switched to biodegradable packaging because reducing its environmental footprint had become a top priority for leadership.
quests.grammarRule: Reason vs Purpose - because, not so that
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Because' explains the existing priority driving this decision. 'So that' would need a modal verb expressing a future goal, which doesn't match this explanation of current priorities.
quests.nativeTip: This explains the reason behind the decision - an existing priority, not a future goal being enabled.
quests.example: The company switched to biodegradable packaging because reducing its environmental footprint had become a top priority for leadership.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: The flight got delayed by six hours, ____ passengers had to find hotels for the night.
quests.completedSentence: The flight got delayed by six hours, so passengers had to find hotels for the night.
quests.grammarRule: Result vs Purpose - so, not so that
quests.ruleExplanation: 'So' introduces this unplanned result. 'So that' would incorrectly suggest the delay was designed to force passengers into hotels, which makes no sense.
quests.nativeTip: Nobody intended this outcome - it's simply what happened as a consequence.
quests.example: The flight got delayed by six hours, so passengers had to find hotels for the night.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: The company released the patch immediately ____ users wouldn't lose any of their saved data.
quests.completedSentence: The company released the patch immediately so that users wouldn't lose any of their saved data.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'So that' introduces this protective purpose, with 'wouldn't' expressing the intended prevention. 'So' would instead suggest this was an unplanned effect.
quests.nativeTip: This was a deliberate, urgent action taken to prevent a problem - a goal, not simply an outcome.
quests.visualAnchor: 🌉 Clause A ──[ so that ]── Clause B
quests.example: The company released the patch immediately so that users wouldn't lose any of their saved data.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: Tom forgot to set a timer, ____ the bread ended up slightly overbaked.
quests.completedSentence: Tom forgot to set a timer, so the bread ended up slightly overbaked.
quests.grammarRule: Result vs Purpose - so, not so that
quests.ruleExplanation: 'So' introduces this unintended result. 'So that' would be illogical here, since nobody set out to overbake the bread on purpose.
quests.nativeTip: Nobody wanted the bread overbaked - this is simply what happened as a result.
quests.example: Tom forgot to set a timer, so the bread ended up slightly overbaked.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: The customer received a full refund ____ the product arrived damaged.
quests.completedSentence: The customer received a full refund because the product arrived damaged.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Because' gives the direct reason for the refund. 'So' would reverse the logic, making the refund the cause of the damage.
quests.nativeTip: This explains the reason for the refund, not an outcome or a goal.
quests.example: The customer received a full refund because the product arrived damaged.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: The product arrived damaged, ____ the customer received a full refund.
quests.completedSentence: The product arrived damaged, so the customer received a full refund.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'So' shows the damage led directly to the refund. 'Because' would only fit if the reason came after the outcome, which isn't the order here.
quests.nativeTip: This time the cause comes first, and the outcome follows.
quests.example: The product arrived damaged, so the customer received a full refund.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: The company now double-checks packaging before shipping ____ future orders won't arrive damaged.
quests.completedSentence: The company now double-checks packaging before shipping so that future orders won't arrive damaged.

quests.nativeTip: This new procedure was put in place with a specific future goal in mind - preventing a repeat problem.
quests.visualAnchor: 🌉 Clause A ──[ so that ]── Clause B
quests.example: The company now double-checks packaging before shipping so that future orders won't arrive damaged.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: The theater will cancel tonight's show ____ ticket sales pick up significantly in the next hour.
quests.completedSentence: The theater will cancel tonight's show unless ticket sales pick up significantly in the next hour.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Unless' shows the cancellation depends on sales failing to improve. 'Because' would incorrectly frame this as an explanation rather than a condition.
quests.nativeTip: The cancellation happens specifically when sales do NOT pick up - which connector already includes that 'not'?
quests.example: The theater will cancel tonight's show unless ticket sales pick up significantly in the next hour.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: ____ the reviews for the restaurant were mostly negative, it stayed fully booked for months.
quests.completedSentence: although the reviews for the restaurant were mostly negative, it stayed fully booked for months.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Although' shows the concession between the negative reviews and the restaurant's popularity. 'Because' would incorrectly suggest the bad reviews caused the full bookings.
quests.nativeTip: Staying fully booked despite bad reviews is the unexpected twist here.
quests.example: although the reviews for the restaurant were mostly negative, it stayed fully booked for months.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: The pilot diverted the flight to the nearest airport ____ a passenger was having a medical emergency.
quests.completedSentence: The pilot diverted the flight to the nearest airport because a passenger was having a medical emergency.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Because' gives the direct reason for the diversion. 'So that' would incorrectly frame the emergency as a future goal rather than an existing cause.
quests.nativeTip: This explains the actual reason for the diversion, which already happened.
quests.example: The pilot diverted the flight to the nearest airport because a passenger was having a medical emergency.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: The old man never returned to the village, ____ too much had changed there since the war.
quests.completedSentence: The old man never returned to the village, for too much had changed there since the war.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'For' introduces the reason in this formal, reflective register. 'Because' would also give a reason but sounds more conversational than this narrative style.
quests.nativeTip: This reads like a formal, reflective narrative - the reason follows a comma in that literary style.
quests.example: The old man never returned to the village, for too much had changed there since the war.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: I'm running late ____ the bus never showed up.
quests.completedSentence: I'm running late because the bus never showed up.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Because' suits this casual, spoken-style explanation. 'For' would sound oddly formal and literary for such a quick remark.
quests.nativeTip: This is a quick, casual explanation - the everyday reason connector fits best here.
quests.example: I'm running late because the bus never showed up.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: The lawyer requested a continuance ____ new evidence could be properly reviewed.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: ____ ticket prices go up next month, Diego is still planning to attend the conference.
quests.completedSentence: even if ticket prices go up next month, Diego is still planning to attend the conference.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Even if' shows his plans hold regardless of a possible price increase. 'Although' would only work if the price increase had already definitely happened.
quests.nativeTip: His plans stay the same no matter what happens with the price - stronger than a simple condition.
quests.visualAnchor: 🌉 Clause A ──[ even if ]── Clause B
quests.example: even if ticket prices go up next month, Diego is still planning to attend the conference.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: The east wing of the museum focuses on ancient artifacts, ____ the west wing showcases contemporary art.
quests.completedSentence: The east wing of the museum focuses on ancient artifacts, whereas the west wing showcases contemporary art.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Whereas' compares these two contrasting sections. 'Although' would suggest one wing exists despite some obstacle, which isn't the relationship being described.
quests.nativeTip: Two different sections are simply being compared here, with neither happening despite the other.
quests.example: The east wing of the museum focuses on ancient artifacts, whereas the west wing showcases contemporary art.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: ____ visitors could navigate more easily, the museum added color-coded signs throughout every floor.

quests.nativeTip: The signs were added with a specific future goal in mind - easier navigation.
quests.visualAnchor: 🌉 Clause A ──[ so that ]── Clause B
